```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(cohortHarmonize)
```

A brief end-to-end example on in-memory data.

```{r}
# --- a target schema (2 variables) ---
ds <- data.frame(
  variable = c("sex", "age"),
  domain   = c("Demographics", "Demographics"),
  type     = c("integer", "integer")
)

# --- one source's raw data + its map ---
raw <- data.frame(
  record_id = 1:3,
  gender    = c("F", "M", "F"),
  dob       = c("1950-01-01", "1960-06-15", "1970-03-20"),
  visit     = c("2016-01-01", "2016-01-01", "2016-01-01")
)
register_recode("sex_text", function(df, cols, param = NULL) {
  s <- tolower(trimws(as.character(df[[cols[1]]])))
  ifelse(s %in% c("f", "female"), 1L, ifelse(s %in% c("m", "male"), 2L, NA_integer_))
})
map <- data.frame(
  target_variable = c("sex", "age"),
  source_columns  = c("gender", "dob;visit"),
  recode          = c("sex_text", "age_from_dates"),
  param           = c(NA, NA)
)

h <- harmonize_source(source_dataframe(raw), map, ds, source_name = "cohortA")
h
coverage_report(h)
```

Read from other formats by swapping the source constructor (e.g. `source_csv("file.csv")`, `source_redcap()`, `source_haven("data.sav")`, or `source_db(conn, table = "t")`). Everything downstream is identical.

See `vignette("creating-a-dataschema")` for the config files, and the README for the federated (multi-site) workflow.
